Transform.description: Represents the position, rotation, and scale of a GameObject in 3D space. Nearly every VRChat interaction involves reading or modifying a Transform to move objects, orient players, or build dynamic world elements.

position.description: World-space position of the object as a Vector3.

rotation.description: World-space rotation of the object as a Quaternion.

localPosition.description: Position relative to the parent Transform.

localRotation.description: Rotation relative to the parent Transform.

localScale.description: Scale relative to the parent Transform.

forward.description: The blue axis (Z+) direction of the object in world space.

right.description: The red axis (X+) direction of the object in world space.

up.description: The green axis (Y+) direction of the object in world space.

parent.description: The parent Transform of this object, or null if it is a root object.

Rotate.description: Applies a rotation around the given axes in degrees.

Translate.description: Moves the transform by the given offset in its local or world space.

LookAt.description: Rotates the transform so its forward vector points at a target position.

SetParent.description: Assigns a new parent Transform, optionally preserving world position.

GetChild.description: Returns the child Transform at the given index.

Find.description: Finds a child Transform by name path. Returns null if not found.

GameObject.description: The fundamental object in every Unity scene. In VRChat worlds, GameObjects hold all components like meshes, colliders, audio sources, and Udon behaviours, and toggling them on or off is one of the most common operations.

activeSelf.description: Whether this GameObject is locally active (ignores parent state).

name.description: The name of the GameObject as shown in the hierarchy.

tag.description: The tag assigned to this GameObject, used for categorization.

layer.description: The layer index this GameObject is on, used for physics and rendering masks.

transform.description: The Transform component attached to this GameObject.

SetActive.description: Enables or disables the GameObject in the scene.

GetComponent.description: Returns a component of the given type attached to this GameObject.

Find.description: Static method that finds a GameObject by name in the scene. Expensive; cache the result.

FindWithTag.description: Static method that finds a single active GameObject with the given tag.

CompareTag.description: Returns true if the GameObject's tag matches the given string. More efficient than comparing tag strings directly.

Vector3.description: A three-component vector used for positions, directions, and scales in 3D space. Vector3 is the workhorse type in VRChat worlds for everything from teleporting players to computing directions between objects.

normalized.description: Returns this vector with a magnitude of 1, preserving direction.

Distance.description: Static. Returns the distance between two points.

Lerp.description: Static. Linearly interpolates between two vectors by t (clamped 0-1).

Slerp.description: Static. Spherically interpolates between two vectors, useful for rotating directions smoothly.
Slerp.example: let dir: Vector3 = Vector3.Slerp(from, to, t)

Cross.description: Static. Returns the cross product of two vectors (perpendicular vector).

Dot.description: Static. Returns the dot product of two vectors. Positive when facing similar directions.

Normalize.description: Static. Returns the given vector with magnitude 1.

Angle.description: Static. Returns the angle in degrees between two vectors.

MoveTowards.description: Static. Moves a point toward a target, capped at a maximum distance per call.
MoveTowards.example: let next: Vector3 = Vector3.MoveTowards(current, target, speed * Time.deltaTime)

Vector2.description: A two-component vector for 2D positions, UV coordinates, and UI layouts. In VRChat worlds it is commonly used for screen-space calculations, texture offsets, and input axes.

normalized.description: Returns this vector with a magnitude of 1.

Distance.description: Static. Returns the distance between two 2D points.

Lerp.description: Static. Linearly interpolates between two 2D vectors by t (clamped 0-1).

Dot.description: Static. Returns the dot product of two 2D vectors.

Angle.description: Static. Returns the unsigned angle in degrees between two 2D vectors.

MoveTowards.description: Static. Moves a 2D point toward a target, capped at a maximum step.
MoveTowards.example: let next: Vector2 = Vector2.MoveTowards(current, target, step)

Quaternion.description: Represents a rotation in 3D space without gimbal lock. In VRChat worlds, Quaternions are used to smoothly rotate objects, orient players, and interpolate between facing directions.

eulerAngles.description: The rotation expressed as Euler angles in degrees (pitch, yaw, roll).

x.description: The X component of the quaternion (not an angle).

y.description: The Y component of the quaternion.

z.description: The Z component of the quaternion.

w.description: The W (scalar) component of the quaternion.

identity.description: Static. The identity quaternion representing no rotation.

Euler.description: Static. Creates a rotation from Euler angles in degrees (X=pitch, Y=yaw, Z=roll).

LookRotation.description: Static. Creates a rotation that looks in the given forward direction.

Slerp.description: Static. Spherically interpolates between two rotations by t. Best for smooth rotation blending.

Lerp.description: Static. Linearly interpolates between two rotations by t. Faster than Slerp but less accurate for large angles.

Angle.description: Static. Returns the angle in degrees between two rotations.

Inverse.description: Static. Returns the inverse (opposite) of a rotation.

RotateTowards.description: Static. Rotates from one rotation toward another, limited by a maximum angle step.

Color.description: Represents an RGBA color with each channel ranging from 0 to 1. Commonly used in VRChat worlds to tint materials, fade UI elements, and drive lighting effects.

a.description: The alpha (opacity) channel (0-1). 0 is fully transparent, 1 is fully opaque.

Lerp.description: Static. Linearly interpolates between two colors by t (clamped 0-1). Great for color fades.
Lerp.example: let fade: Color = Color.Lerp(Color.red, Color.blue, t)

LerpUnclamped.description: Static. Linearly interpolates between two colors without clamping t.
LerpUnclamped.example: let c: Color = Color.LerpUnclamped(start, end, t)

Rigidbody.description: Adds physics simulation to a GameObject, enabling gravity, collisions, and forces. In VRChat worlds, Rigidbodies drive throwable pickups, physics puzzles, and any object that needs to move realistically.

velocity.description: The linear velocity of the rigidbody in world-space units per second.

angularVelocity.description: The angular (rotational) velocity in radians per second.

mass.description: The mass of the rigidbody in kilograms.

drag.description: Linear drag coefficient. Higher values slow movement faster.

angularDrag.description: Rotational drag coefficient. Higher values slow rotation faster.

isKinematic.description: When true, the rigidbody is not driven by physics but can still affect other bodies.

position.description: The position of the rigidbody in physics space.

rotation.description: The rotation of the rigidbody in physics space.

AddForce.description: Applies a force vector to the rigidbody, pushing it over time.

AddTorque.description: Applies a torque vector, causing the rigidbody to spin.

MovePosition.description: Moves the rigidbody to a position, respecting physics interpolation.

MoveRotation.description: Rotates the rigidbody to a rotation, respecting physics interpolation.

Collider.description: Defines the collision shape of a GameObject for physics and trigger detection. In VRChat worlds, colliders are essential for player interaction zones, trigger volumes, and physical boundaries.

enabled.description: Whether this collider is active. Disabled colliders are ignored by physics.

bounds.description: The world-space bounding box of the collider.

isTrigger.description: When true, the collider acts as a trigger zone instead of a solid surface.

attachedRigidbody.description: The Rigidbody attached to this collider's GameObject, or null if none.

ClosestPoint.description: Returns the closest point on the collider surface to a given position.

Raycast.description: Casts a ray against this collider and returns hit information.
Raycast.example: // Use Physics.Raycast for general raycasting instead

AudioSource.description: Plays audio clips in the scene with spatial positioning, volume, and pitch control. In VRChat worlds, AudioSources power background music, sound effects, ambient audio, and interactive sound triggers.

clip.description: The AudioClip currently assigned to this source.

pitch.description: Playback speed/pitch multiplier. 1 is normal, 2 is double speed.

loop.description: Whether the audio restarts automatically when it reaches the end.

isPlaying.description: True if the source is currently playing a clip.

mute.description: When true, the source is silenced but continues playing internally.

playOnAwake.description: Whether the source starts playing automatically when the scene loads.

spatialBlend.description: Controls 2D (0) to 3D (1) spatial blending. 3D audio fades with distance.

Play.description: Starts playing the assigned clip from the current time position.

Stop.description: Stops playback and resets the time position.

Pause.description: Pauses playback at the current position. Resume with UnPause.

UnPause.description: Resumes playback from where it was paused.

PlayOneShot.description: Plays a clip once without interrupting the current clip. Ideal for overlapping sound effects.

Animator.description: Controls animation state machines and blend trees on a GameObject. In VRChat worlds, Animators drive doors opening, buttons pressing, environment changes, and any visual state transitions.

speed.description: Global playback speed multiplier for all animations on this Animator.

enabled.description: Whether this Animator component is active.

SetBool.description: Sets a boolean parameter in the Animator controller by name.

SetFloat.description: Sets a float parameter in the Animator controller by name.

SetInteger.description: Sets an integer parameter in the Animator controller by name.

SetTrigger.description: Activates a trigger parameter, causing a one-shot transition.

GetBool.description: Returns the current value of a boolean Animator parameter.

GetFloat.description: Returns the current value of a float Animator parameter.

GetInteger.description: Returns the current value of an integer Animator parameter.

Play.description: Plays an animation state by name immediately.

CrossFade.description: Smoothly transitions to an animation state over a given duration in seconds.

Mathf.description: A collection of static math functions and constants. Mathf is used everywhere in VRChat worlds for clamping values, interpolating animations, computing trigonometry, and generating oscillating effects.

Infinity.description: Positive infinity. Useful as an initial value when searching for a minimum.

Deg2Rad.description: Multiply by this constant to convert degrees to radians.

Rad2Deg.description: Multiply by this constant to convert radians to degrees.

Epsilon.description: The smallest float value greater than zero. Useful for float comparisons.

Abs.description: Returns the absolute (non-negative) value of a float.

Ceil.description: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the value, as a float.

CeilToInt.description: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the value, as an int.

Clamp.description: Restricts a value to lie between min and max (inclusive).

Clamp01.description: Restricts a value to lie between 0 and 1.

Floor.description: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to the value, as a float.

FloorToInt.description: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to the value, as an int.

Lerp.description: Linearly interpolates between a and b by t (clamped 0-1).

LerpUnclamped.description: Linearly interpolates between a and b without clamping t.

Max.description: Returns the larger of two float values.

Min.description: Returns the smaller of two float values.

MoveTowards.description: Moves a value toward a target by at most maxDelta per call.
MoveTowards.example: let val: float = Mathf.MoveTowards(current, target, speed * Time.deltaTime)

PingPong.description: Oscillates a value between 0 and length as the input increases.

Pow.description: Returns base raised to the given exponent.

Round.description: Rounds to the nearest integer, returning a float.

RoundToInt.description: Rounds to the nearest integer, returning an int.

Sign.description: Returns 1 for positive values, -1 for negative values, and 0 for zero.

Sin.description: Returns the sine of an angle in radians. Great for oscillating effects.

Cos.description: Returns the cosine of an angle in radians.

Tan.description: Returns the tangent of an angle in radians.

Sqrt.description: Returns the square root of a value.

Log.description: Returns the natural logarithm (base e) of a value.

Repeat.description: Wraps a value into the range [0, length), like modulo but works with floats.

Player.description: Represents a VRChat player in the instance. The Player API lets you read player information like display name and position, teleport players, modify movement settings, and check network roles like master or instance owner.

displayName.description: The player's visible VRChat display name.

playerId.description: The unique integer ID assigned to this player for the current instance.

isMaster.description: True if this player is the current instance master (first player or next after master leaves).

isLocal.description: True if this player is the local user running this Udon script.

isInstanceOwner.description: True if this player created the current VRChat instance.

GetPosition.description: Returns the player's current world-space position.

GetRotation.description: Returns the player's current world-space rotation.

TeleportTo.description: Teleports the player to a position and rotation. Only works on the local player.

SetVelocity.description: Sets the player's movement velocity. Useful for launch pads and boost zones.

GetBonePosition.description: Returns the world position of a specific avatar bone (e.g., head, hand).

GetBoneRotation.description: Returns the world rotation of a specific avatar bone.

IsPlayerGrounded.description: Returns true if the player is currently standing on a surface.

IsUserInVR.description: Returns true if the player is using a VR headset (false for desktop users).

Immobilize.description: Prevents or allows the local player from moving. Pass true to freeze, false to unfreeze.

EnablePickups.description: Enables or disables the player's ability to pick up VRC_Pickup objects.

SetJumpImpulse.description: Sets the upward force applied when the player jumps.

SetRunSpeed.description: Sets the player's running movement speed.

SetWalkSpeed.description: Sets the player's walking movement speed.

SetGravityStrength.description: Sets the gravity multiplier for the player. 1 is normal, 0 is zero-gravity.

Networking.description: Provides static methods for VRChat's networking system, including ownership management and local player access. Ownership determines which client has authority to sync an object's state to other players.

IsOwner.description: Returns true if the given player is the network owner of the specified GameObject.

SetOwner.description: Transfers network ownership of a GameObject to the specified player. Required before modifying synced variables.

LocalPlayer.description: Returns the VRCPlayerApi for the local user running this script.

GetOwner.description: Returns the VRCPlayerApi of the current network owner of a GameObject.

IsNetworkSettled.description: Returns true once all synced data has been received after joining an instance. Use this to delay initialization.

IsInstanceOwner.description: Returns true if the local player is the instance creator.

IsMaster.description: Returns true if the local player is the current instance master.

IsClogged.description: Returns true if the network send queue is backed up. Useful for throttling sync requests.

Time.description: Provides read-only static properties for tracking elapsed time, frame deltas, and frame counts. In VRChat worlds, Time values drive animations, cooldown timers, movement smoothing, and any frame-rate-independent logic.

time.description: Time in seconds since the scene loaded (affected by time scale).

deltaTime.description: Time in seconds since the last frame. Multiply by this for frame-rate-independent movement.

fixedDeltaTime.description: The fixed time step in seconds used by physics updates.

unscaledTime.description: Time in seconds since the scene loaded, ignoring time scale changes.

unscaledDeltaTime.description: Frame delta time ignoring time scale. Useful for UI animations.

frameCount.description: The total number of frames that have been rendered since the scene started.

realtimeSinceStartup.description: Real wall-clock time in seconds since the application started.

timeSinceLevelLoad.description: Time in seconds since the current scene (level) was loaded.

Debug.description: Provides static logging methods that write to the Unity console. In Nori, prefer the built-in log(), warn(), and error() shortcut functions which are more concise and support string interpolation directly.

Log.description: Writes an informational message to the Unity console.

LogWarning.description: Writes a warning message (yellow) to the Unity console.

LogError.description: Writes an error message (red) to the Unity console.
